cases.name: literal-is-always-valid
cases.covers: A literal query skips the pattern check entirely, flags and all.

cases.name: regex-with-diacritics-is-refused
cases.covers: The one rejected flag combination. Diacritic folding is a property of the folded text plane and a regex runs on the raw one, so this asks for something that does not exist.
cases.message: Diacritic-sensitive matching is not available for regex patterns (regex runs on the raw text plane).

cases.name: diacritics-is-reported-before-a-bad-pattern
cases.covers: Both wrong at once reports the flag, because that is the one a caller can fix without rewriting the pattern.
cases.message: Diacritic-sensitive matching is not available for regex patterns (regex runs on the raw text plane).

cases.name: regex-lookaround-is-refused
cases.covers: A dialect refusal reaches the query validator with its own issue intact.

cases.name: regex-backreference-is-refused
cases.covers: The other dialect refusal, through the same path.

cases.name: empty-pattern-is-refused
cases.covers: An empty regex is refused where an empty literal is merely fruitless.

cases.name: key-defaults-to-full-mode
cases.covers: An absent mode is full, and the cursor key says so.

cases.name: key-spells-the-rects-mode
cases.covers: The spelling in the key is the wire spelling. A cursor minted by one implementation and replayed against another compares as a string, so a synonym here is a refusal no caller could diagnose.

cases.name: key-separates-every-flag
cases.covers: Each flag moves the key, so a cursor is not transferable across a toggle.

cases.name: key-separates-regex-from-literal
cases.covers: Same text, different plane, different identity.

cases.name: cursor-resumes-its-own-query
cases.covers: The accepting case, so the refusals below are not vacuous.

cases.name: cursor-from-another-query-is-refused
cases.covers: The key pins the query. Resuming under a different one would scan the wrong needle.

cursor.message: search cursor belongs to a different query — restart the search

cases.name: cursor-from-before-a-mutation-is-refused
cases.covers: The sequence pins the content. Resuming over mutated pages could serve text a redaction just removed.

cursor.message: document changed since this search cursor was issued — restart the search

cases.name: cursor-beside-a-conflicting-start-page-is-refused
cases.covers: The cursor owns the position. Letting it quietly win would hand back matches from a part of the document the caller did not ask about.

cursor.message: `from` conflicts with the cursor — omit it when resuming

cases.name: cursor-beside-the-matching-start-page-is-allowed
cases.covers: A startPage that agrees with the cursor is redundant rather than wrong.

cases.name: a-cursor-that-is-not-json-is-refused
cases.covers: The opaque contract cuts both ways: nothing is read out of a malformed one.

cases.name: a-cursor-of-another-version-is-refused
cases.covers: A future format is refused rather than reinterpreted through this one.
